A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the algal cultivation in the wastewaters from municipal wastewater treatment plants is a promising option to reduce the nutrient load in the wastewater treatment plant, and to produce biofuel feedstocks from wastewater.
algal growth can be used to remove the nutrients and metals from the wastewater in the MWTP and the algal biomass can be harvested for biofuel feedstock.
the centrate, which is a wastewater generated in sludges centrifuge, is a good source to culture algae for biofuel production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
algal growth in centrate is a viable option of nutrient reduction in MWTPs.
the wastewater centrate can be an effective growth medium for algal biomass production, which can be used for biofuel production.
the wastewater treatment process can be optimized to generate a high nutrient wastewater stream for algae cultivation.
